title: Peatland ACTION FW02 Field Ecologists Framework
description: NatureScot work to improve our natural environment in Scotland and inspire everyone to care more about it. We work to ensure that all nature in Scotland - our key habitats and landscapes, all our green space and our native species - are maintained, enhanced and bring us benefits. Our priority is a nature-rich future for Scotland and an effective response to the climate emergency. Peatland ACTION funding - from Scottish Government - primarily supports on-the-ground peatland restoration activities and is open for applications from eligible land managers who have peatlands that would benefit from restoration. There are no geographical restrictions or target areas for Peatland ACTION funding. Peatlands are an iconic part of the Scottish landscape and have many benefits for people and nature. Healthy peatlands provide important ecosystem services including storing and sequestering carbon, supporting unique and specialised biodiversity, improving downstream water quality, and regulating water flow to provide natural flood management. In contrast, damage to peatlands reduces or reverses these benefits. For example, degraded peatlands release stored carbon and are a major global source of greenhouse gas emissions. Peatland ACTION is led and funded by Scottish Government and delivered in partnership with NatureScot, Cairngorms National Park Authority, Loch Lomond & the Trossachs National Park Authority, Forestry and Land Scotland, and Scottish Water. Since 2012, Peatland ACTION has set over 66,000 hectares of degraded peatland on the road to recovery, but this effort needs to accelerate rapidly in the coming years to help address the twin crises of the climate emergency and biodiversity loss. The appointed Field Ecologists will work with the Peatland ACTION Technical Team and Project Officers located across Scotland to help support species and ecological survey requirements for Peatland ACTION restoration sites.

title: Stonehaven Promenade Improvement Works
description: Aberdeenshire Council are inviting tenders for Stonehaven Promenade Improvement works. Aberdeenshire Council require a Contractor to construct the Works which will involve widening the existing pavements to create a safer active travel route for pedestrians and wheelchair users to access the recreational/leisure facilities. New crossing points will be created and raised to pavement levels to improve accessibility for pedestrians and wheelchair users in crossing from one side of the road to the other. The plans also include designing and installing new parapet barriers along the seafront and resurfacing works to the Promenade.

title: USCG Yard: Sensors and Meters
description: Solicitation for Supplies This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items, prepared in accordance with the format in subpart 12.6 of the FAR Part 12 - Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services | Acquisition.GOV and as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 2126406Y152141466 applies and is used as a Request For Quote (RFQ). This solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2024-05, dated 22 May 2024. It is anticipated that a Best Value purchase order shall be awarded as a result of this synopsis/solicitation. All responsible sources may submit a quotation, which if timely received, shall be considered by this agency. Best Value will be evaluated by who can provide the complete requirement, who meets the required time frame, and by price. All vendors providing a quotation must either have an active SAM.gov registration or provide proof they have submitted their entity for registration. Payments are NET 30 and will be made in accordance with the FAR 52.232-25 Prompt payment clause 52.232-25 Prompt Payment. | Acquisition.GOV. The U.S. Coast Guard, Surface Forces Logistics Center (SFLC) intends to award a Firm Fixed Price Purchase Order. All quotes shall be emailed to Chelsea Colson via Chelsea.L.Colson@uscg.mil and shall be received no later than 10/6/2026 at 0700 (Eastern). All email quotes shall have 2126406Y152141466 in the subject of the email. The United States Coast Guard Surface Forces Logistics Center, please review attachment for a list of requirements, items, descriptions, cage codes, etc. Packaging Specifications Packaging requirements are mandatory to meet warehouse inventory requirements. Each item shall be individually packaged for inventory to match the Coast Guard �Unit of Issue,� (example: EA, LB, HD). The minimum packaging method used is commercial packaging; defined as the way items are packaged, sold, and shipped to the public over the counter provided the package matches the �Unit of Issue.� Smaller items only (i.e. Bolts and Screws) can be packaged with multiple items in one package or container providing the marking also includes the quantity in the container. For example, a package bag or box can have 10, 25, or 50 bolts, if that package is marked IAW marking requirements below, plus the quantity. Marking Requirements All packages, boxes, bags or containers shall be clearly marked/labeled with the following information: Item noun name Our stock number (13 digit) Manufacturer Part Number Cage Code (if known) Purchase Order/Contract number Unit of Issue Quantity If a single item cannot be packaged in one container, each container shall be marked �Box 1 of 2,� �Box 2 of 2,� etc. Failure to comply with all packaging and marking requirements without prior approval will result in material being returned at vendors� expense for correction. Bar coding is not required. Label example: Item Name Stock Number Purchase Order/Contract Number Unit of Issue & Quantity Delivery Address and Terms Access to some drawings may be Export-Controlled and require any recipient to be registered in the Joint Certification Program (JCP) through DLA to receive the drawing. Any proposed substitution must be accompanied by a Specification Sheet to undergo evaluation by the requiring officials for compatibility to the Requirement. Total cost shall have delivery and any Freight charges included. Shipping: FOB Destination Required All material must be shipped to: U.S. Coast Guard YARD Baltimore Facilities Management 2401 Hawkins Point Road Receiving Room, Bldg. 88 Baltimore, MD, 21226 Material must be accompanied by an itemized packaging list securely attached to the outside of the shipment. All packing lists shall cite the Purchase Order Number with the packaging in such a manner to ensure identification of the material provided. Material shall be packed for shipment using Military Packaging, for examples in packaging please reference MIL-STD-2073-1E. Material must be packaged in such a manner as to afford adequate protection to the item against corrosion, deterioration, and physical damage during shipment from the supply course to Surface Forces Logistics Center locations. Packaging shall provide adequate protection for warehouse storage and shipments from the warehouse. All materials shall be marked in accordance with MIL-STD-129R and barcoded unless otherwise authorized by the Contracting Officer. All material will have the Purchase Order Number, National Stock Number (if applicable), Vendor name and Part Number clearly marked on the exterior of all material shipped. All Deliveries are to be made Monday through Friday between the hours of 7:00AM to 1:00PM. Invoicing in IPP It is a requirement that all invoicing for Purchase Orders will now be entered and processed through https://www.ipp.gov. All invoices must contain the following information if possible: Coast Guard Purchase Order Number Vendors� Invoice Number Cage Number/Cage Codes Purchase Order Item Number Description of Supplies or Services Unit Price Extended Totals Shipping costs will be indicated as a separate line item on the invoice (if applicable). Shipping costs of $100 or more must be accompanied by a separate freight invoice when submitting an invoice(s) for payment (if applicable). To submit an invoice, vendor must have access to www.ipp.gov. To gain access, please indicate if you don�t have an account so the issuing office can establish one for you. title: Technologická dodávka pro úpravnu pitné vody Stjepan Polje
description: Předmětem plnění veřejné zakázky je dodávka technologického vybavení pro úpravnu pitné vody v lokalitě Stjepan Polje v rámci projektu „Efektivnější zásobování pitnou vodou v municipalitě Gračanica“. Zakázka navazuje na již zpracovanou realizační projektovou dokumentaci, která byla připravena v předchozí fázi projektu. Tato dokumentace představuje výchozí technický podklad pro realizaci dodávky technologie. Předmětem aktuálního plnění je zejména: • zpracování dílenské / dodavatelské dokumentace technologické části, dodávka, doprava, montáž a propojení technologických zařízení, • technologické elektroinstalace, MaR, PLC a SCADA, • revize, protokoly, tlakové, funkční a další zkoušky, • individuální vyzkoušení a 72hodinové komplexní vyzkoušení, • dokumentace skutečného provedení, • provozní řád pro zkušební a trvalý provoz, • školení obsluhy, • 12měsíční zkušební provoz včetně měsíčních návštěv technologa a laboratorního monitoringu, • publicita projektu, • záruční servis. Předmět plnění veřejné zakázky je podrobně popsán v příloze č. 1 této ZD, dále je specifikován položkovým rozpočtem (příloha č. 2 ZD) a smlouvou (příloha č. 3 ZD).

title: Germany – Rural areas mapping services – Kartierung Monitoring und Risikomanagement - StDeOe.7022 Amphibien, StDeOe.7023 Offenlandvogelarten, StDeOe.7024 Vegetation, StDeOe.7025 Phengaris
description: Los 1 - StDeOe.7022 Amphibien: Im Zuge des Donauausbaus Straubing – Vilshofen, Teilabschnitt 1, Straubing – Deggendorf, wird ein Monitoring und Risikomanagement für LBP-Maßnahmen durchgeführt. In diesem Zusammenhang müssen Daten zum Besiedlungserfolg von Amphibien sowie zur Entwicklung der zugehörigen LBP-Maßnahmenflächen erhoben werden. Es handelt sich hierbei um die Arten Knoblauchkröte (Pelobates fuscus) und Laubfrosch (Hyla arborea). Die Vertragslaufzeit erstreckt sich von Januar 2027 – November 2028. Im Rahmen dieser Arbeiten sind die Ergebnisse digital aufzubereiten und ein Erläuterungsbericht sowie eine Fotodokumentation zu erstellen. Los 2 - StDeOe.7023 Offenlandvogelarten: Im Zuge des Donauausbaus Straubing – Vilshofen, Teilabschnitt 1, Straubing – Deggendorf, wird ein Monitoring und Risikomanagement für ausgewählte LBP-Maßnahmen durchgeführt. In diesem Zusammenhang muss 2027 eine Revierkartierungen zur aktuellen Bestandssituation der Offenlandvogelarten Kiebitz (Vanellus vanellus) und Großer Brachvogel (Numenius arquata) durchgeführt werden. Die Vertragslaufzeit erstreckt sich von Februar bis Oktober 2027. Im Rahmen dieser Arbeiten sind die Ergebnisse digital aufzubereiten und ein Erläuterungsbericht sowie eine Fotodokumentation zu erstellen. Los 3 - StDeOe.7024 Vegetation: Im Zuge des Planfeststellungsverfahrens Donauausbau Straubing – Vilshofen, Teilabschnitt 1, Straubing – Deggendorf, wird ein Monitoring und Risikomanagement für ausgewählte LBP-Maßnahmen durchgeführt. Dieses Monitoring ist aufgegliedert in ein vegetationsbezogenes Monitoring und ein maßnahmenbezogenes Monitoring. Im Zusammenhang des vegetationsbezogenen Monitorings müssen Biotop- und Nutzungstypen, sowie FFH-Kartierungen inkl. Bewertung für die Lebensraumtypen 91E0*, 91F0, 9170 und 6210 durchgeführt werden. Außerdem erfolgt eine Kartierung der Art Lindernia procumbens sowie Arten der Teichried-, Teichboden und Zwergbinsengesellschaften. Im Rahmen des maßnahmenbezogenen Monitorings sind vegetationsökologische Untersuchungen zu, Gehölzaufwuchs, Baumartenzusammensetzung und Störzeiger, sowie weitere standörtliche Erfassungen durchzuführen. Des Weiteren erfolgen bodenkundliche Kartierungen (Fingerprobe) verschiedener LBP-Maßnahmenflächen. Die Vertragslaufzeit erstreckt sich von 2027 bis 2028. Im Rahmen dieser Arbeiten sind die Ergebnisse jährlich digital aufzubereiten und ein Erläuterungsbericht sowie eine Fotodokumentation zu erstellen. Los 4 - StDeOe.7025 Phengaris: Im Zuge des Planfeststellungsverfahrens Donauausbau Straubing – Vilshofen, Teil-abschnitt 1, Straubing – Deggendorf, wird ein Monitoring und Risikomanagement für ausgewählte LBP-Maßnahmen durchgeführt. In diesem Zusammenhang müssen Daten zur aktuellen Bestandssituation des Dunklen Wiesenknopf-Ameisenbläulings (Phengaris nausithous) auf Referenzflächen sowie zur Entwicklung von LBP-Maßnahmenflächen erhoben werden. Im Rahmen dieser Arbeiten sind die Ergebnisse digital aufzubereiten und ein Erläuterungsbericht sowie eine Fotodokumentation zu erstellen.

title: Research Project on Service Navigation Support for Seniors
description: Title: Research Project on Service Navigation Support for Seniors - 100032783 The Service Navigation Support for Seniors project will have two components. The first component, Component A will review the accessibility of information on support services available to seniors and/or their caregivers across all federal, provincial and territorial (FPT) jurisdictions and to identify common barriers. The objective of Component A is to understand what support services are the most frequently requested across the 14 FPT jurisdictions and why the access rate for information is more elevated, especially as it relates to barriers in accessing them. The second component, Component B, will use the results from Component A and identify, in collaboration with FPT Officials a number of case studies to analyse the mechanisms through which seniors and/or their caregivers learn about and/or access support services aiming to build awareness and improve access to service navigation supports. This would also include policy recommendations for jurisdictions to consider in enhancing service navigation support for seniors.

title: Thermal releases: Review of international regulatory practices and options for incorporation into a compliance and licensing framework.
description: Please return offers by email to solicitation-demandedesoumission@cnsc-ccsn.gc.ca Canada is seeking offers from qualified Offerors to provide professional services to review if and how thermal risk assessments (TRAs) are being conducted across the electrical power generation industry domestically and internationally, and if there are any existing regulatory frameworks addressing management of thermal effluent. The work will identify gaps in the standardized application of TRA methods and provide recommendations where applicable for improvement in standardization of TRAs for the nuclear power plants in Canada. The scope includes a critical evaluation of thermal effects literature for reliability and relevance for being able to inform a TRA, and the generation of an updated database of thermal effects thresholds for Canadian relevant species fish, and invertebrate species in the marine and freshwater environment. The scope of this project also includes reviewing and compiling data on regulatory approaches used by different facilities utilizing once-through cooling system technology (e.g., nuclear power plants, oil and gas plants, etc.), nationally and internationally, with respect to thermal risk assessment and the derivation and application of thermal thresholds.

title: Independent (Geoscience) Advisory Group on the long-term management of used nuclear fuel in a Deep Geological Repository (Phase V)
description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission (CNSC) has a requirement to build and maintain independent and contracted geoscientific expertise, consistent with international best practice, through an independent scientific advisory group. The group supports the CNSC’s regulatory preparedness by providing independent advice on the long-term management of used nuclear fuel in Canada and by supporting technical reviews of regulatory documentation expected from the Nuclear Waste Management Organization (NWMO) in relation to its Deep Geological Repository (DGR) project. The purpose of this advance contract award notice (ACAN) is to signal the CNSC’s intention to award a contract for these services to: Carleton University 1125 Colonel By Drive Ottawa, ON K1S 5B6 Canada T +1 613 520 2600 www.carleton.ca Before awarding a contract, however, the CNSC would like to provide other suppliers with the opportunity to demonstrate that they can satisfy the requirements set out in this ACAN, by submitting a statement of capabilities within the posting period for this ACAN, which is 15 calendar days. If, during the posting period, other potential suppliers submit a statement of capabilities that meets the requirements set out in this ACAN, the CNSC may proceed to a full tendering process via the Government Electronic Tendering Service or by inviting bids directly from suppliers. If no other supplier submits, on or before the closing date, a statement of capabilities meeting the requirements set out in the ACAN, a contract will be awarded to the above-noted supplier. 2.0 BACKGROUND The NWMO has developed the Adaptive Phased Management (APM) plan for the long-term management of Canada’s used nuclear fuel. The NWMO initiated the formal regulatory review of their proposed DGR (through an integrated IA, which includes the initial CNSC licence) in early 2026. The ultimate goal is the centralized containment and isolation of Canada’s used nuclear fuel within a deep geological repository. DGRs rely on the host rock and engineered barriers to contain and isolate the wastes from the biosphere for hundreds of thousands to millions of years. Currently, the NWMO has selected the Wabigoon Lake Ojibway Nation - Ignace site in Ontario for the implementation of the project. Currently, the CNSC is developing regulatory preparedness for technical reviews of regulatory documentation expected from the NWMO in support of their DGR project. As part of building and maintaining independent knowledge, the CNSC continues independent and contracted geoscientific research. It is also international best practice for the regulator to have an independent scientific advisory group assist in regulatory preparedness and provide independent advice to the regulator. In 2014, the IAG was formed to respond to this need. Phase I commenced from 2014 to 2018. As part of the Phase II of the IAG took place from 2018 to 2021. The IAG continued in Phase III and IV from 2021 to 2024, and 2024 to 2027, respectively. This SOW outlines the requirements for Phase V of the IAG. 3.0 SCOPE OF WORK AND EXPECTED OUTCOMES The IAG is expected to develop an annual work plan in conjunction with CNSC staff, in-line with the state of the Impact Assessment for the NWMO’s DGR project and consistent with the scope of CNSC’s activities. Based on the tasks identified in the work plan, the IAG will provide independent geoscientific advice to the CNSC related to the long-term management of used nuclear fuel in Canada. The annual work plan will include one or more of the following tasks: • Provide input and advice to CNSC’s technical reviews as requested, specific to NWMO’s integrated impact assessment (including licence application), in particular to the technical reports associated with and/or supporting the safe case for DGR project. • Review CNSC’s past, current, and future research plans in the context of international best practices in repository research, and identify opportunities and recommendations for future research. • Review the NWMO’s geoscientific research by using annual reports and /or other technical information documents, and attending geoscience seminars. • Conduct focused review of NWMO and/or CNSC reports, journal and conference papers in specific areas of geoscientific importance in consultation with IAG and CNSC The IAG will carry out these tasks in accordance with the Terms of Reference 4.0 ESTIMATED PERIOD AND VALUE OF CONTRACT The proposed contract is for a period of 3 years, from April 1, 2027. The estimated value of the contract is $450,000. Applicable taxes are extra. 5.0 MINIMUM MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS Any interested supplier must demonstrate by way of a statement of capabilities that all members of the group meet the following minimum mandatory requirements: • The supplier must not have been employed by the Nuclear Waste Management Organization (NWMO) within the previous five years. • Academic qualifications of team members shall include graduate degrees from a recognized university (MSc or PhD) in the field of geomechanics, hydrogeology, geology, and geochemistry, geophysics, and any other area deemed necessary by the CNSC as identified during regulatory reviews. • 25 years of experience in field of geomechanics, hydrogeology, geology, and geochemistry • 10 years of experience providing advice in the field of geoscience and radioactive waste management on specific topics including but not limited to deep geological repository, geomechanics, hydrogeology, geology, and geochemistry, geophysics, and any other area deemed necessary by the CNSC as identified during regulatory reviews. 6.0 JUSTIFICATION FOR THE PRE-SELECTED SUPPLIER Carleton University is considered unique because it has an established network of specialized individuals with expertise in the technical fields required for this work, including geomechanics, hydrogeology, geology, geochemistry, geoscience, radioactive waste management, deep geological repositories, site characterization, safety case development, and the long-term safety assessment of geological disposal. While there may be other suppliers with general geoscience expertise, this requirement also requires access to a coordinated group of experts who can provide independent, third-party advice on NWMO submissions related to licensing, while maintaining familiarity with the CNSC’s technical review needs and the Canadian regulatory context. A further key requirement is that the experts must be fully independent from the NWMO. Specifically, they must not have previously performed work for the NWMO and must not have any current or previous relationship with the NWMO as an employee, contractor, or advisor in the past 5 years. This independence requirement significantly limits the availability of alternative sources of supply. Carleton’s established network is therefore uniquely positioned to provide the required breadth of specialized expertise while meeting the strict independence requirement for this contract. These subject matter experts have extensive experience, demonstrated by a track record of providing advice, and conducting research, relevant to the field of nuclear waste disposal. Carleton University has previously provided independent geoscientific advice to the CNSC, demonstrating familiarity with regulatory expectations, review processes, and the provision of objective technical assessments. In addition, the proposed supplier has thorough and up-to-date knowledge of the ongoing research and development (R&D) activities, as well as the licensing framework and supporting technical work associated with the NWMO DGR program. This includes awareness of evolving methodologies, safety case development practices, and site-specific investigations being undertaken as part of the siting and upcoming regulatory review process. title: ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE: Pointe-de-Longueuil Construction Manager
description: Canada Lands Company CLC Limited (the “Company”) on behalf of Build Canada Homes (“BCH”) intends to retain a construction management services firm (the “Construction Manager”) in respect of the development project for the lands located at the Pointe-de-Longueuil in Longueuil, Quebec (the “Development Project”). The Company is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (“APN”) to provide interested parties with preliminary information regarding the Development Project as well as the competitive procurement process (the “Procurement Process”) that the Company expects to undertake to retain the Construction Manager. This APN is not part of the Procurement Process, and does not constitute a bid solicitation, tender, or procurement process of any kind in respect of the procurement of the Construction Manager or the Development Project. No agreement or contract will be entered into based on this APN. The issuance of this APN is not to be considered in any way a commitment by the Company to undertake the Procurement Process or the Development Project, and the Company reserves the right to modify the Procurement Process or the Development Project, in whole or in part, in its sole discretion, including based on any comments received from interested parties pursuant to this APN. This APN is not to be considered as a commitment to issue a subsequent solicitation or award contract(s) for the Construction Manager or Development Project described herein. The Development Project involves the development of approximately 23 hectares (57 acres) of land located at the former Transport Canada site known as Pointe-de-Longueuil in Longueuil, Québec (the “Site”). The Site will be transformed into a mixed-use community comprising residential, commercial, institutional, and community uses, including a housing project forming part of the first wave of housing projects to be undertaken by or on behalf of BCH. Through the Procurement Process, the Company intends to retain the Construction Manager to provide pre-construction services and assume responsibility for managing and coordinating the work, procuring and administering trade contractors, and delivering the Development Project, together with such other services as may be required by the Company from time to time. Subject to municipal approvals, remediation and infrastructure works are anticipated to commence in early 2027. The initial phase of the Development Project will focus on enabling works, environmental remediation, and horizontal infrastructure required to support future development phases, including site preparation and earthworks, utility installations, stormwater, sanitary sewer and watermain systems, roads, sidewalks, district energy infrastructure, landscaping, and related works. The Development Project is expected to have an estimated total value range of between $100 million and $200 million. The Development Project is expected to be delivered in phases, and the Construction Manager may be retained for all phases or for any individual phase that is planned by the Company.

title: KOY Riihimäen Jäähallin vanhan jäähallin IV- ja LTO-saneeraus
description: KOY Riihimäen Jäähallin vanhan jäähallin IV- ja LTO-saneeraus KOY Riihimäen Jäähalli (jäljempänä "Hankintayksikkö" tai "Tilaaja") pyytää tarjouksia jäähallin IV- ja LTO-järjestelmän saneerauksesta. Saneerauksilla pyritään parantamaan hukkalämmön hyödyntämistä ja kohteen ilmanvaihdon toimivuutta. Urakkaan: Osa 1: sisältyvät uusi ilmanvaihtokone ja ilmanvaihtotyöt, sisältäen vanhan IV-laitteiston purkutyöt sekä liitynnät 2022 asennetun kylmätekniikkakontin lämmitys- ja jäähdytysputkistoihin. Hankintaan sisältyy optiona Osa 2: LTO-järjestelmän saneeraus, jolla pystytään hyödyntämään kylmätekniikkakontilla syntyvää lauhdelämpöä huoltorakennuksen lämmityksessä. Tätä varten rakennetaan maanalaiset lämmitysputkistot piha-alueelle ja tehdään tarvittavat muutokset huoltorakennuksen lämmönjakolaitteistoon. Osan 2 toteutuessa ilmanvaihtokontin sisäinen sähkökattila jää pois ja ilmanvaihdon vara/lisälämmönlähteenä käytetään kaukolämpöä. Lauhdelämpöteho on riippuvainen siitä miten koneita joudutaan käyttämään jäänteon yhteydessä. Siksi mukana vara/lisälämpöratkaisu. Rakennusautomaatiojärjestelmää (RAU) koskevat lähtötiedot ovat saatavilla nykyiseltä järjestelmätoimittajalta. Järjestelmässä käytetään toimittajan tarjolla olevaa ajantasaisinta ohjelmisto- ja laiteversiota. IV-kontin valvonta-alakeskus (VAK) uusitaan kokonaisuudessaan osana urakkaa. Uusinnan yhteydessä automaatiomoduulit, I/O-laitteet sekä muut valvonta-alakeskuksen keskeiset komponentit korvataan uusilla. Tarjoajan tulee huomioida kokonaisuus ja siihen liittyvät laite-, ohjelmointi-, käyttöönotto- ja dokumentointityöt tarjouksessaan. Rakennustyöt on suunniteltu aloitettavaksi maalis–huhtikuussa 2027. Tarkempi aikataulu sovitaan Tilaajan ja valitun Urakoitsijan kesken ennen sopimuskauden alkamista. Halli on varattu urakan ajaksi urakoitsijan käyttöön, eikä käyttäjällä ole muuta toimintaa kohteessa urakan aikana. Hankinnan kohde ja toimeksianto on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön liitteissä. Tilaaja edellyttää, että urakoitsija on tutustunut rakennuskohteeseen Tilaajan nimeämän edustajan kanssa ennen tarjouksen jättämistä. Kohteeseen tutustumisesta sovittava erikseen Eero Takalan kanssa 050449790, eero.takala@riihimaki.fi Hankintamenettely on avoin menettely ja kilpailutuksen perusteella valitaan sopimukselle yksi (1) urakoitsija. Tässä hankinnassa kokonaistaloudellisen edullisuuden perusteena käytetään halvinta hintaa. Tarjouspyynnössä laadulle asetut vähimmäisvaatimukset mahdollistavat vertailun ainoastaan hinnalla. Kaikki hankintaa koskevat vaatimukset on esitetty tarjouspyynnössä ja sen liitteissä. Tarjous on sitova ja se tulee laatia suomen kielellä. Hankintayksikkö ei sitoudu tiettyihin hankintamääriin, eikä sopimus muodosta Palveluntuottajalle yksinoikeutta hankinnan toteuttamiseen.,

title: Evaluering av tilskuddsordninger for nasjonale minoriteters språk og kultur
description: Kulturdirektoratet forvalter fem tilskuddsordninger for å styrke nasjonale minoriteters språk, kultur, identitet og egenorganisering. De nasjonale minoritetene i Norge er kvener/norskfinner, skogfinner, romanifolk/tatere, romer og jøder. Ordningene er sentrale virkemidler for aktiv samfunnsdeltakelse og styrking av språk og kultur. På oppdrag fra Kommunal- og distriktsdepartementet lyser Kulturdirektoratet nå ut en ekstern evaluering av disse ordningene. Formålet med evalueringen er å få kunnskap om hvorvidt, i hvilken grad og på hvilken måte tilskuddsordningene bidrar til å oppfylle målene som er satt og hvordan de eventuelt kan videreutvikles for bedre å styrke nasjonale minoriteters språk og kultur. Oppdragstaker skal vurdere om ordningene er effektive med hensyn til ressursbruk, organisering og måloppnåelse.

buyer: Department of Agriculture Food and the Marine
title: Ireland – Laboratory services – Analysis of samples to establish the presence of nematode pests
description: The Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine (DAFM) is the National Plant Protection Organisation (NPPO) of Ireland. DAFM performs phytosanitary controls across the country, in a wide range of locations including farms, forests, nurseries and parks. These phytosanitary controls are in line with International Standards for Phytosanitary Measures (ISPM’s), and in compliance with the Plant Health Regulation (EU) 2016/2031, Commission Implementing Directive (EU) 2019/2072 and the Official Controls Regulation (EU) 2017/625. These controls are performed by a variety of divisions including Horticulture and Plant Health, Forestry Inspectorate, Crop Policy, Evaluation and Certification, and Import Control Operations. These controls are supported by the Plant Science Division (PSD) which performs diagnostics across bacteriology, nematology, entomology, virology, and mycology on samples resulting from Official Controls and Other Official Activities. PSD is designated as the National Reference Laboratory for all these areas including nematology, in accordance with EU regulations. Any laboratory successful in this tender will be nominated as an Official Laboratory for nematology for Ireland. DAFM undertakes a significant amount of sampling in nematology to support our agricultural industry and requires the provision of supplemental diagnostics. The successful laboratory will be expected to provide diagnostics on approximately 1500 samples across a range of matrices including soil, peat, and plant material. The diagnostics required will focus on plant parasitic and free-living nematodes, with particular focus, but not limited to, EU Quarantine and Regulated non-Quarantine species. The successful laboratory will be expected to provide results, reports, and advice within designated turnaround times and be accredited in compliance with EU regulations. The provision of this service will assist DAFM in carrying out the required phytosanitary actions to maintain Irelands high plant health status, and to protect our agricultural industry and environment.

title: Finland – Forestry services – Metsänhoidon palvelusopimus 2027-2028 (2029-2030)
description: Mäntsälän kunta pyytää tarjoustanne metsänhoidon palvelusopimuksesta, jonka tavoitteena on turvata talous- ja puistometsien laadukas metsänhoito, hakkuumahdollisuuksien täysimääräinen ja suunnitelmallinen hyödyntäminen talousmetsissä, maisemanhoito ja virkistysmahdollisuuksien huomioiminen sekä tilaajan edunvalvonta metsänhoitoon liittyvissä asioissa. Metsäpalvelusopimus laaditaan vuosille 2027-2028 ja sopimusta voidaan jatkaa yhdellä kahden (2) vuoden mittaisella optiokaudella. Mäntsälän kunta omistaa noin 870 hehtaaria metsää, jota hoidetaan vuosille 2024–2033 laaditun metsäsuunnitelman mukaisesti. Metsäsuunnitelma on tarjouspyynnön liitteenä. Suunnitelman keskeinen periaate on, että hakkuut ja metsänhoitotyöt kilpailutetaan erikseen, jotta kunta saa puukaupasta parhaan tuoton ja töistä kustannustehokkaan toteutuksen. Palveluntuottaja suunnittelee, kilpailuttaa ja valvoo metsänhoitotyöt kunnan lukuun. Työt tilataan kunnan vuosisuunnitelman mukaisesti. Alihankinta on sallittu, eikä tarjoajalta edellytetä omaa konekalustoa. Tarjouspyynnöllä annetut arviot perustuvat metsäsuunnitelmaan ja siinä määriteltyyn hakkuiden toteumaan. Arvioissa on huomioitu vuosille 2027-2033 suunnitellut hakkuut: - hakkuukertymä 2000-2500 m3/vuosi - puukaupan tulot 90 000-100 000 euroa/vuosi - hakkuut n. 20 ha/vuosi - metsänhoitotyöt, kuten taimikonhoito, raivaus, istutus tai muut vastaavat työt n. 15-25 ha/vuosi. Vuosittaiset määrät vaihtelevat sen mukaan mitä hakkuita ja töitä kulloinkin toteutetaan. Tilaaja ei sitoudu tiettyihin hankintamääriin, vaan hankinnat tehdään tilaajan tarpeen ja määrärahojen puitteissa. Metsäsuunnitelman ulkopuoliset pienehköt hankintahakkuut (infra-alue, myrskytuho tai muut vastaavat) palveluntuottaja suorittaa puun myynnin parhaaseen mahdolliseen markkinahintaan. Markkinakartoitus ja hankinnan osiin jakaminen: Hankinnan valmisteluvaiheessa on toteutettu markkinakartoitus, joka kuvataan hankinta-asiakirjoissa hankintaa koskevissa lisätiedoissa. Hankintayksikkö kilpailuttaa metsänhoidon palvelusopimuksen yhtenä kokonaisuutena ja valitsee sopimuskaudelle yhden (1) palveluntuottajan. Osiin jakamatta jättämisen perusteena on hankintayksikön oma sekä markkinakartoituksen infotilaisuudessa saatu alan toimijoiden näkemys, että hankinta muodostaa toiminnallisesti luontevan kokonaisuuden, jonka jakaminen osiin ei ole tarkoituksenmukaista. Hankinnan osiin jakaminen lisäisi hallinnollista taakkaa ja koordinointia, nostaisi siten kokonaiskustannuksia logististen ja operatiivisten päällekkäisyyksien vuoksi, sekä hajottaisi vastuita, mikä voisi heikentää metsänhoidon laadun ja aikataulujen hallintaa. Yhtenäinen hankintakokonaisuus edistää kustannustehokkuutta, vastaa markkinan rakennetta eikä rajoita kilpailua.

buyer: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF
title: RNA sequencing and whole genome sequencing services
description: NOTICE OF INTENT � SOLE-SOURCE ACQUISITION Notice No.: 75N98027Q00020 The National Institutes of Health (NIH), National Cancer Ibstitute (NCI), intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price Purchase Order to Plasmidsaurus Inc. for RNA sequencing and whole genome sequencing services for various wild-type, drug-treated cell lines and samples related to CRISPR research. Description of the Requirement The primary objective of this study is to investigate common lymphoma-related translocations involving MYC, BCL6, or BCL2, while also examining copy number alterations and making CNV calls for genes of interest. To achieve this, RNA sequencing will be provided for samples generated in the Staudt laboratory. RNA sequencing is essential for characterizing genome edits and conducting transcriptomic analysis. By utilizing Plasmidsaurus, a faster and more scalable alternative to traditional sequencing methods based on the latest Oxford Nanopore Technologies platform, we aim to generate results that will deepen our understanding of cellular mechanisms involved in B-cell lymphoma and guide future downstream experiments. RNA sequencing and Whole-genome sequencing are required to observe the effects of various drugs on gene expression, identify pathways, and discover novel pathways. Justification for the Proposed Sole-Source Acquisition The Government intends to solicit from a single source pursuant to FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. Plasmidsaurus uses the latest Oxford Nanopore Technologies platform, a faster, more scalable alternative to traditional sequencing. Using the latest Oxford Nanopore Technologies platform ensures accurate sequencing, which is crucial for reproducible experiments which will significantly advance our understanding of, and treatment for, B-cell lymphoma, which is vital to cancer research at the National Cancer Institute. Response Information This notice is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals. However, interested parties that believe they can meet the Government's requirements may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the required preventive maintenance and remedial repair services for the specified instrument and meet all applicable technical and operational requirements. The Government will review timely submissions to determine whether another responsible source is capable of satisfying the requirement and whether a competitive acquisition is appropriate. The Government anticipates making an award approximately five (5) calendar days after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another responsible source can satisfy the requirement. Capability statements must be submitted electronically to verne.griffin@nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. EDT on November 6, 2026. Please reference Notice No. 75N98027Q00043 in the subject line of the submission.

title: Call for Solutions - Europe Area Inventory
description: The Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) is seeking a mature commercial solution, automated computer vision/sensor workflows, rapid mobile inventory scanning technologies, and streamlined data integration platforms capable of executing SKU-level perpetual inventory counts and real-time validation across complex retail floors and storage warehouses in their 32 European stores. DeCA European commissary operations span varied physical configurations, including high-volume customer sales floors, chilled and frozen storage, backroom prep stations, and remote warehouse staging areas. Retail items include standard domestic packaged goods, European-sourced items (EAN barcode format), compressed UPC (6/7/8-digit), fresh meats and cheeses with variable weights (random weight labels), and bulk goods with Price Look-Up (PLU) codes. DeCA is seeking to have all inventories completed from April �May. Please see attached document for desired schedule and examples of inventory markings. DeCA is actively advancing an enterprise-wide modernization roadmap, including an upcoming transition to an SAP-supported enterprise resource planning (ERP) environment. Consequently, DeCA requires a commercial partner whose technical architecture can scale and grow with the Agency�bridging current legacy catalog/flat-file data exchange formats today while natively enabling modular, direct integration into DeCA's target SAP digital core in subsequent years. Our objective is to establish a long-term partnership with a provider whose technology, service model, and commercial terms align with our commitment to delivering reliable, value driven solutions. DeCA seeks solutions that will provide this support for up to five total years, requesting that solutions propose a Period of Performance (PoP) that reflect customary commercial processes. The Government reserves the right to adjust the proposed PoP to align with mission requirements, funding availability, and applicable regulatory limitations, including structuring the award as a base period with one or more option periods at the Government's discretion. The attached Call for Solutions letter contains additional information regarding the request for Commercial Solutions Briefing. Please be sure to download a copy of the letter as there is an attachment within the document that can only be opened if downloaded.

title: Infrarakentamisen valvonnan ja tilannekuvan sovelluksen hankinta
description: Infrarakentamisen valvonnan ja tilannekuvan sovelluksen hankinta Kaupunkiympäristön toimiala (KYMP) on toteuttamassa Infrarakentamisen valvonnan ja tilannekuvan sovelluksen hankintaa. Järjestelmä hankitaan ohjelmistopalveluna (SaaS). Sillä tuetaan katujen, puistojen ja muiden yleisten alueiden infrahankkeiden seurantaa valmistelusta takuuajan päättymiseen, erityisesti urakan toteutusvaiheen hallintaa, dokumentointia ja viestintää kenttäolosuhteissa. Järjestelmää käyttävät kaupungin rakennuttajat ja suunnittelijat sekä urakoitsijat ja suunnittelu- ja valvontakonsultit. Käyttäjiä on tavoitetilassa noin 400, ja urakkavaiheessa olevia hankkeita on vuosittain noin 200. Hankinta sisältää ohjelmistopalvelun käyttöoikeudet, ylläpidon ja tuen sekä kiinteähintaisen käyttöönottoprojektin. Ohjelmistopalvelu on toimitettava lopulliseen hyväksymistestaukseen viimeistään 12 kuukauden kuluttua sopimuksen allekirjoittamisesta. Lisäksi hankinta sisältää tarvittaessa erikseen tilattavia koulutus-, jatkokehitys- ja asiantuntijapalveluja. Sopimus on voimassa toistaiseksi. Hankinnan tausta ja kohde on kuvattu tarkemmin liitteessä Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus.,

description: The purpose of this Statement of Work (SOW) is to outline the scope, deliverables, and responsibilities for the relocation of gear, machinery, and storage equipment from two existing warehouses (Bldgs. 54938/54805; 15160 Scrub Jay St Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, FL 32920) into an adjacent facility (Hangar AO; 60530 Hangar Rd Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, FL 32920) that is approximately 1/4 mile away. This project requires careful inventory management, safe transport of delicate machinery, and precise placement to ensure minimal operational downtime for Detachment 3. Equipment to be moved includes, but is not limited to: sewing machines, cargo parachutes, personnel parachutes, boat motors, floatation rafts, Vidmar/toolboxes, supply cabinets, printers, storage lockers, and air drop-able rescue equipment packages that consist of jet skis and boats. The target move-in date is 2 November 2026. (Target move in date is an outdated figure. Please disregard this detail in the statement of work.) The government is instead requesting completion as soon as possible and no later than 30 days after award. See statement of work (SOW) attachment for full project description. Site Visit for this effort is mandatory as the governmnet will not be proving measurements of buildings and items to be transported. Contractors are responsible to take all nessecary measurements themselves. title: Parking Lot and Paved Areas Recapitalization
description: SCOPE OF WORK Work to be completed under this contract involves the removal of existing asphalt paving, reprofiling the grading of designated areas shown in the drawings, upgrading some drainage infrastructure (curbs, manholes, among others), and installing a new asphalt surface. The replacement must be performed as per the drawings and specifications provided. The contractor must provide all the required materials, equipment before/during/after installation, and labour for installation, and manage the project requirements following the National Building Code of Canada. Project progress meetings are required at regular intervals with the owner, consultant, and the contractor; the specific intervals will be determined in more detail at the kick-off meeting. Further project details are contained in the project plans and specifications. This project shall be completed by March 31, 2027.

title: Reverse Osmosis System Replacement – AAFC Summerland Research and Development Centre
description: Title: Reverse Osmosis System Replacement – AAFC Summerland Research and Development Centre Description: The Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada (AAFC) Summerland Research and Development Centre located in Summerland, BC has a requirement for the replacement of the existing centralized Reverse Osmosis (RO) systems with a new Type II Deionization water purification system. In addition to replacement of the systems, the project includes replacing 50mm supply water piping with 40mm piping and reconnection to existing piping to make good the work, as well as all electrical and ancillary work to support the new installation. Basis of selection: This is a two phase selection process. Bidders responding to this ITT are to submit in two phases. Phase One qualification covers only the qualifications and experience of the Bidders. Following the evaluation of Phase One submissions, Bidders will be advised of the result of the assessment of their submission and the status of the Phase Two tender. Phase Two Bidders will be provided an Invitation to Tender (ITT) for the financial evaluation in relation to the specifications and drawings. A combination of the Phase One and Phase Two submissions constitutes the final bid. Initially, Bidders are invited to submit their qualifications in the first phase of the selection procedure. Only the Phase One information asked for in the ITT is to be included in Phase One submissions, and evaluation of Phase One submissions will be carried out only on the Phase One information requested.
